note: The iterative completion ladder. Simple cases first: a tier is only declared complete when its own cases reach their expected terminal state, no blocking uncertainty is hidden inside a single payable, and a named reviewer has signed the outcome. Higher tiers add exactly one new source of complexity each, so a failure always points at one operator, one config value, or one missing document. `gate` uses the same predicate language as knowledge/review_procedure.json.
promotion_rule: A tier passes only on its own gate: every example case reaches its expected terminal state.
A tier may not be promoted over a case whose outcome was produced by a parameter nobody supplied.
Passing a tier certifies only the outcome class it names; it certifies nothing about the next tier.
A tier that can produce a single payable must also produce it with a computed confidence and a rule trace.

tiers.name: One number, nothing assumed
tiers.purpose: Prove the pipeline can pay a fully specified claim without inventing a single input.
tiers.exit_evidence: A payable whose every deduction is traceable to an assessor figure plus one policy term, with no defaulted input.
tiers.must_not: Do not certify this tier with a case that has an unresolved blocking uncertainty, or where the franchise was defaulted to zero because nobody answered.

tiers.name: Computed deductions
tiers.purpose: Add the operators that compute rather than copy: the depreciation year index, the component categories, the special-part cap and the rescue ceiling.
boundary_cases_required: year index 4 (no depreciation), 5 (first 5%), and the 25% ceiling
glass and lamp glass in the same itemised assessment as an ordinary part
battery or tyre where the cap binds but the vehicle is still too new to depreciate
rescue below, exactly at, and above the 20% ceiling
tiers.exit_evidence: The depreciation figure matches the year index for every part, and the cap binds before any age schedule does.
tiers.must_not: Do not stack the 50% battery/tyre cap with the age schedule to make this tier pass - that collision belongs to T3.

tiers.name: Branch boundaries
tiers.purpose: Decide which engine the case belongs to, and prove the boundary is strict rather than rounded.
boundary_cases_required: repair plus rescue below, exactly at, and one unit above 75% of value
whole-vehicle theft at 59, 60 and 61 days, with and without title transfer
standalone glass with and without the endorsement; glass broken with other damage
parts stolen after an accident, which is an exclusion, not a theft branch
salvage retained versus insurer takes title
tiers.exit_evidence: Equality at 75% stays partial; sixty days is total and fifty-nine is pending; a non-compensable peril returns zero with the reason, not a blank.
tiers.must_not: A declared branch that contradicts the evidence is refused here, not honoured.

tiers.name: The ratio is live
tiers.purpose: Introduce under-insurance, where the correct answer is a set of sourced scenarios rather than one number.
boundary_cases_required: ratio below one in partial damage with a franchise: two scenarios, one blocking uncertainty
total loss where the ratio must not be applied a second time after the insured-sum cap
battery or tyre on a vehicle whose depreciation year index has reached five
ratio exactly one, where both orders coincide and a single payable is honest
tiers.exit_evidence: Every scenario is labelled with the order that produced it, and the confidence drops to the single-interpretation confidence of the unresolved ordering.
tiers.must_not: Do not average the scenarios, do not pick the flattering one, and do not apply the ratio twice in total loss.

tiers.name: The contract has not been read yet
tiers.purpose: Handle claims where the law is settled and the policy wording is missing - the engine must name the artefact it needs.
boundary_cases_required: an endorsement token with no printed schedule: coverage yes, amount no
a percentage franchise with no named calculation base or source version
a glass endorsement whose wording conditions payment on being insured at market value
an unresolved salvage disposition
tiers.exit_evidence: The refusal names the document, the coverage line and the field within it that is missing, and no amount is produced.
tiers.must_not: Never fill a contractual gap with a rate remembered from another insurer, a blog table, or the same company's different product version.

tiers.name: Two policies, one loss
tiers.purpose: Add allocation: contribution between insurers, prior indemnity, recourse, and the split between an ordinary and a non-conventional vehicle.
boundary_cases_required: another policy already paid part of the loss: this insurer pays its ratio of its own commitment
the insured released the responsible party: review, not arithmetic
risk intensified without notice: escalate, because the premium-ratio operator is not implemented
a non-conventional vehicle where correspondence assessment is absent: refuse rather than invent a ratio
tiers.exit_evidence: Each payer's share, each cap and each created right of recourse is stated separately, and no party pays twice.
tiers.must_not: Do not model a third-party cap inside a body branch, and do not treat an Article 8 excess as automatically a debt of the at-fault driver.

tiers.name: Anything not yet certified
tiers.purpose: The default state for any case outside T0-T5: new peril, new product, new insurer, missing annual parameters, or a rule the graph does not carry.
tiers.exit_evidence: The file states which rung of the ladder it fell off and what would put it back on.
tiers.must_not: Reaching this tier is not an error; presenting its answer as a payment decision is.
